title: Daswandh in the code
hookLine: giving a tenth of earnings for the Guru's cause

lines: ONE MORE PILE, AT THE FRONT.
cards: Payday. The money lands, and before it does anything else, it gets sorted. Rent here.
Groceries there. Something for the phone bill, something for the car. Every household has its own version, on paper, in an app or in someone's head.

Now add one more pile at the front of the line, set aside before rent, not after the fun. Not a tip from whatever's left over, but a share taken first and given away. Sikhs have a plain name for that share.

teach.b: Daswandh means a tenth part. In Sikh teaching, it's a tenth of one's earnings, given for the Guru's cause, and it belongs to the way of life the code sets out for a Sikh. Three things to notice.
First, what it comes out of: earnings, honest work. Sikh teaching joins remembering the Name, earning honestly, and sharing what you have, and daswandh sits where earning and sharing meet.

Guru Nanak puts it in one line, on Ang twelve hundred forty-five, in paraphrase: the one who eats what they earn by their own work and gives some of it away from their own hand, that one recognizes the path.
From your own hand, not someone else's pocket. Second, where it goes.
The Guru's cause is wide. It can fund the langar, where anyone can sit and eat, keep gurdwaras open, support schools, and pay for relief when disaster strikes.
Some Sikhs give it in money, others give part of it in time, serving in the kitchen or teaching children. Communities differ on how strictly to count.

teach.h: A MEASURE THAT MAKES A HABIT.

teach.b: A tenth is concrete: small enough to live with, large enough to notice. Giving whatever is left over depends on mood.
A tenth, set aside first, turns sharing from a feeling into a habit, and the habit into a quiet partnership with everyone the langar feeds.

how: Sikhs who keep daswandh set aside a tenth of their earnings for the Guru's cause, giving to gurdwaras, the langar, education and relief, and some give part of it as time and service.

games.q: what does “daswandh in the code” mean?
o: a tenth of the harvest paid to the local ruler
a tenth of honest earnings, given for the Guru's cause
a yearly tax a gurdwara charges every member

p: earn, and give from your own hand

s: daswandh is whatever is left at the end of the month
it is a tenth of earnings, set aside for the Guru's cause.
daswandh comes out of honest earnings
it sits where earning honestly and sharing meet.
daswandh can only fund the gurdwara building
the Guru's cause is wide: the langar, schools, relief and more.

games.q: you've just been paid and want to give daswandh. when does the share come out?
o: at the end, if anything is left.
games.why: the point of a set measure is that sharing becomes a habit, not a mood. and yesterday, the code ruled out lucky days.

practice: Bring to mind what came to you lately, money, time or skill, and without doing any math, picture a share of it set apart first, before the other piles.
Then let one place it could go come to mind, a food bank, a neighbor, a gurdwara kitchen, an hour for someone stretched thin, and if you pray, offer it quietly with the word Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Daswandh in the code. A tenth part of honest earnings, given for the Guru's cause, set aside first. Today's word.

orig.note: Punjabi: a tenth part, given from earnings for the Guru's cause.

carryVoice: Your line: a tenth. Small enough to live with, large enough to notice. See you tomorrow.
